the_one_open_question.statement: The campaign's floor is 0.4116484014x (ARCH.V10CL896X09, sealed 1/15, double-witnessed by its G10 arm) and every child at or below it spends an EXCISION -- depth x vocabulary, which wave 30's fitted allocator prices at 4.44 cases, the most expensive pair in the model.  The cheapest pair is mlp x vocabulary at 1.17.  No child has ever been built on that pair below CL896, because the CL ladder has no rung between 640 and 896.
the_one_open_question.what_settles_it: a CL768 body and its vocabulary ladder.  CL768 + K=9,216 lands at 0.4133826104x -- the floor's depth, reached with NO excision at all, on the mildest measured interference in the model.  If it holds a case, intelligence survives below the floor by a route the campaign never took; if it holds none, 0.4116x is a property of the parent and not of the axis pair, and that is the stronger negative this campaign has been unable to state.
three_outcomes_declared_in_advance: V9CL768 holds at least one case -- the mlp x vocabulary route reaches the floor's depth without an excision, and the deep family's excision was a tax it did not have to pay.

V9CL768 holds zero but CL768 holds two or more -- the body survives the mlp cut and the vocabulary ladder kills it anyway, which makes the 0.41x band a property of the vocabulary axis at this parent size rather than of the excision.

CL768 itself holds zero or one -- the mlp cliff between 640 and 896 sits ABOVE 768, the floor attack dies at the body, and every rung below it is a formality that this wave will still build and still read, because a ladder on a dead body is how DEEP_RECORD 8.5's decay law was measured in the first place.

Block 9 is a conv block and its MLP scales with --ff: at ff=768 the same excision removes 3 x 1024 x 768 = 2,359,296 rather than 3 x 1024 x 896 = 2,752,512, so it costs 6,558,720 and not 6,951,936.

Two sealed numbers, both to the byte, before any prediction below was written.

children.prediction_reasoning: THE MIDPOINT OF THE CAMPAIGN'S SHARPEST MLP TRANSITION.  ARCH.CL640 reads 0/15 at 0.6404971x and ARCH.CL896 reads 4/15 at 0.6884308x, and nothing has ever been built between them.  Two accounts disagree and they disagree by four cases.  (a) LINEAR: the transition is graded and 768 is halfway, so 2.  (b) CLIFF: wave 30's reading that the mlp axis 'flattens onto the sealed 896' makes 896 a plateau edge and puts the whole drop just below it, which reads 3 or 4.  (c) The inverse cliff puts the drop just above 640 and reads 0 or 1.  Predicting 2 is the account with no cliff in it, which is the account this campaign has the least evidence for on this axis and therefore the one worth being wrong about.

stated_deviations.deviation: K4 -- the score-bilinear joint q/k lead -- is NOT built this wave and no partial version of it is.
stated_deviations.why: the order funds it 'if budget'.  It has no module, no driver and no precedent in this tree, and its exact-4x storage claim cannot be realised in a stock checkpoint on this parent: contracting head_dim for q and k alone is not a stock config axis when v shares it, and zero-padding is on the kill list.  It is therefore a research probe with a materialised dense export whose storage claim is arithmetic rather than a loader count, and a probe of that shape costs a module, a driver, a build and a review.  Wave 40 spends that budget on the ten core children and the C1 repair instead, and says so here rather than reporting the omission afterwards.

stated_deviations.deviation: K3(b) -- the ORTHO-PAIR soft arm on the living pair -- is NOT built.
stated_deviations.why: its base, ARCH.X07KV6JQC, is a wave-17-to-22 child and is not on the share; no retention manifest kept it.  The arm needs that body, a conditioned capture through it and a re-solve, which is a body build plus a capture plus a solve plus a review -- not the 'zero storage delta, one build' the inventory prices it at, because the inventory prices the SOLVE and not the reconstruction of the base.  This is recorded as a cost correction to the inventory, not as a decision that the class is closed.  Its registration still says build regardless of census, and it still stands.

stated_deviations.deviation: K3(c) -- Monarch's first cell -- is NOT built.
stated_deviations.why: same shape of problem as K4.  A Monarch factorisation is not expressible in a stock Lfm2ForCausalLM config, so the child is either a custom-module research probe (ADDENDUM 12: no ARCH id, no loader ratio, and A8 F-LANDMARK has been stuck in exactly that state for eighteen waves for want of a loader) or a materialised dense export whose storage claim is arithmetic.  Wave 40 does not have the budget to do that properly AND read ten children, and doing it improperly would add a tenth unpriced probe to an estate whose problem is unpriced probes.
no lambda ladder runs this wave.  Wave 38 said a wave that wants to move n has to spend two solves; wave 40 spends none on that axis and says so rather than counting an arm.

stated_deviations.why: standard invocation, parent FIRST, as every wave since 32.  The subset is named in the note and is chosen to cover both new bodies, the K1 ladder's three depths and the tie child beside its deletion control, because a benchmark column that does not carry the controlled pair cannot be read against the review.
